name: stella
why: An Atari 2600 emulator opens a door into vintage console hardware and cartridge-era programming, with real retro appeal.

brief.what_it_is: Stella is a multi-platform emulator for the Atari 2600 VCS, the 1977 home console. It runs Atari 2600 game cartridge images on a PC so you can play classic games on a desktop. The project's site describes it as released under the GNU General Public License. The homepage lists ports to AcornOS, AmigaOS, DOS, FreeBSD, IRIX, Linux, OS/2, MacOS, Unix and Windows. The README says the Stella Users Manual lives in the repository's docs subdirectory. The README does not describe its inputs and outputs beyond running games.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage frames it as a way to "enjoy all of your favorite Atari 2600 games on your PC". It also points readers to information about the Atari 2600, emulation and homebrew development.

commands_seen.context: macOS Terminal workaround in the README for Gatekeeper blocking the app as unverified. Removes the quarantine attribute from Stella.app. The alternative is right-click or Control-click the app, choose Open, then confirm Open.

brief.install_notes: On macOS, Gatekeeper may refuse to open the downloaded app with the message "Stella cannot be opened because Apple cannot verify it is free from malware." The README gives two workarounds: right-click (or Control-click) Stella.app, choose Open, and confirm, which only needs doing once; or run the xattr command above against the app path. No accounts, runtimes or hardware are mentioned in the pages I read. The brew formula's executable is named stella.
brief.standout: It has been around since 1995 and is still maintained by a team after its original Linux author. The project now runs on donations ("Stella is now DonationWare") while staying under the GPL. Its README is blunt about scope: it asks people not to report issues for platforms other than PC and RetroN 77, such as Libretro forks.
brief.status: Appears maintained but I could not confirm recent activity. The homepage says "Site Updated January 3, 2025" and the copyright runs to 2025. The GitHub README I fetched shows no release date or commit date, and I did not check the releases or commit history.
brief.caveats: The README says the Stella Team is not responsible for forks on other platforms, including Libretro, and asks that issues for those be kept out of the main tracker. On macOS, the downloaded app may be blocked by Gatekeeper until one of the workarounds is applied. The homepage notes that Stella is now donation-supported. The brew description and scout notes say it has retro appeal, but I found nothing in the pages I read to back that up beyond the emulator's purpose.
quotes: Stella is a multi-platform Atari 2600 VCS emulator which allows you to play all of your favourite Atari 2600 games on your PC.
Please do **not** report issues regarding platforms other than PC and RetroN 77 (e.g. Libretro) here.
